cases.note: 预设句英文·Ontario software grad

turns.text: Ontario college grad, software dev, no job yet — can I stay?
turns.answer:
Yes, you can stay through a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but your time in Canada is strictly limited by its expiry date. The permit length depends on your study program duration: if it was two years or more, you get three years; otherwise, it matches your program length (minimum eight months). You must apply within 180 days of receiving your completion confirmation and meet a CLB 5 language requirement for college graduates. 

While Ontario currently lists 52 open postings for software developers, finding employment is necessary to extend your stay or transition to permanent residence once the PGWP expires. Without a job offer, you cannot simply remain in the country after that permit ends unless you qualify for another pathway.

Key conditions to keep working legally:
- Your study program must have been at least eight months long.
- You can only receive one PGWP in your lifetime.
- The permit allows you to work for any employer without an LMIA.
